children.objective: Explore outer-loop OpenMP parallelization in src/candidate.cpp, using the run threads argument as a hard CPU-thread budget rather than assuming OMP_NUM_THREADS is the budget. Keep the baseline per-element arithmetic unchanged to isolate threading effects; handle small n and uneven partitions without omissions, and write every output. Compare suitable scheduling and parallel-region policies with repeated official wall-clock measurements, and validate varied inputs. Do not modify other files or the compiler, harness, or protocol.
children.subject: OpenMP parallelization of independent options

children.objective: Keep this track single-threaded to isolate per-element gains, and compare a lower-risk path with an aggressive one. First test algebraically equivalent arithmetic reductions (for example, Horner evaluation of the existing CND polynomial) while retaining the baseline scalar logf, sqrtf and expf calls; check whether the frozen compiler already performs the proposed reductions. Contrast that with SIMD using only features that compile on the frozen target, including bounded vector math approximations only if needed. Do not alter compiler flags or add libraries. Preserve scalar fallback and tail handling, process every entry, and validate the full tolerance on varied per-element inputs—not just the published performance constants. Measure each path separately with the official harness.
children.subject: Contrast arithmetic-preserving and SIMD math optimizations
